summary: Read-only investigation identified a delivery-contract gap and a missing invalidation path; no production source edits. Isolated registered worktree mcp-response-alert-worker11-20261121 bound to main d702352ef705f9991ac1cb14dc15a13cce78aa44; remote main verified at same SHA.
nextAction: Resolve with Lead the delivery/acknowledgment contract for lost replies and precise invalidation design before claiming no-loss semantics; inspect baseline job and coordinate native Windows availability. Preserve existing behavior until a design can prove bounded lost-invalidation recovery, canonical CAS fencing and the specified delivery semantics; then implement and test under a non-overlapping lease.
evidence: At d702352, Client/SignalR/Client.fs:109-122 performs loadWithSnapshot then takeResponseAlertsAt on every eligible visible response, including GetJobResult via lines 1249-1256. Existing ReviewWorkflowTests.fs:6332-6336 asserts one remote fetch for a no-alert poll. ReviewWorkflow.fs:1619-1633 explicitly commits consumption before returning the alert and states loss of the response loses the alert; this conflicts with task acceptance requiring no lost STOP under missed replies. LedgerStore.fs:1029-1053 emits invalidation only for changed agents/*.json state projections, while queue/clear at ReviewWorkflow.fs:1573-1609 changes the response-alert queue, so current agent-state invalidation is not itself a queue-change notification. Five Linux completed GetJobResult tool round trips were 929, 894, 912, 843, 800 ms, not per-stage timings or representative concurrency. Windows device KRUSO disconnected. .NET 11.0.100 Linux Release baseline job a9167dafeccb4b2ba8e7372ffe93b2d1 running; initial --no-restore job 18f91d4636544db99130ec119512a4a5 returned no test output and is not test evidence.
